title: A letter about the future
paragraphs:
Dear Nurzhan,

I hope you are well in Almaty and that your exams went better than you expected! It is almost summer here in Uralsk, and I am sitting at my desk with a cup of tea, thinking about everything that is going to happen in the next few months. I have so many plans — I wanted to write and tell you all of them, because you always give me good advice.

First — the big news. I am going to do an internship this summer at a tech company in Astana. The company is called DataBridge Solutions — they build data analysis tools for businesses. I applied in February and they offered me a place last week. I cannot believe it! I am going to work there for six weeks, from the fifteenth of June to the twenty-fifth of July. The work is going to be real — not just making coffee, but writing actual code. I am so excited and a little nervous at the same time.

After the internship, I am going to spend two weeks in Semey with my family. I know two weeks is not very long, but the internship is too important to skip. My parents understand. My mum is going to cook every day and my dad is going to take me fishing at the river — that is our tradition. I am going to rest, eat well, and recharge before the new semester.

In August, the whole family is going to travel to Turkestan — all seven of us, including my grandparents. We have never been there together, and my grandmother has always wanted to see the Yasawi Mausoleum. She is seventy-three years old, so we are not going to wait any longer. My grandfather is going to drive from Semey. We are going to stay for three days. I am going to take my camera and photograph everything.

For next year at WKU, I have two goals. First, I am going to apply for the WKU Academic Excellence Scholarship — the deadline is in September. Second, I am going to join the Computer Science Club. They meet every Thursday evening to work on group projects. I think it is going to help me make more friends and improve my programming skills at the same time.

So that is my plan, Nurzhan! What are you going to do this summer? Are you going to stay in Almaty or travel somewhere? I really hope we are going to meet in person before September — maybe in Astana while I am at the internship? Write back soon.

Your friend,
Kairat

dialogue.text: I'm going to do an internship at DataBridge Solutions in Astana for six weeks.

dialogue.speaker: Bakyt
dialogue.text: An internship already? You're only in your second year!

dialogue.speaker: Kairat
dialogue.text: I know — but I applied early. It's going to be real work — actual coding, not just coffee!

dialogue.speaker: Bakyt
dialogue.text: And after the internship? Are you going to go home to Semey?

dialogue.speaker: Kairat
dialogue.text: Yes, for two weeks. Then my whole family is going to travel to Turkestan in August.

dialogue.speaker: Bakyt
dialogue.text: The whole family? That sounds like a great trip! And for next year at WKU?

dialogue.speaker: Kairat
dialogue.text: I'm going to apply for the Academic Excellence Scholarship and join the CS Club.

dialogue.speaker: Bakyt
dialogue.text: What am I going to do? I haven't decided yet — maybe look for a job in Almaty.

dialogue.speaker: Kairat
dialogue.text: That's a big decision! When are you going to make up your mind?
